title: Security+
description: CompTIA Security+ SY0-701 exam prep across 5 weighted domains, with PBQ scenario drilling.

units.title: General Security Concepts
units.gate: Given an unfamiliar scenario, name which CIA-triad property and which control type/category apply, and explain a PKI or authentication choice without hand-waving the mechanism.

objectives.text: CIA triad, non-repudiation, and the AAA security model
Security control types (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and control functions (preventive, detective, corrective, deterrent, compensating, directive)
Cryptographic fundamentals: symmetric vs asymmetric encryption, hashing, digital signatures, key exchange
objectives.labPrompt: Generate a self-signed TLS certificate with OpenSSL and inspect its fields with openssl x509 -text -noout.

objectives.text: PKI basics: certificates, certificate authorities, chains of trust, revocation (CRL/OCSP)
objectives.labPrompt: Open a site in your browser, view its certificate chain, and trace it from the leaf certificate up to the root CA.

objectives.text: Authentication methods and factors: MFA, biometrics, SSO, federation
Access control models: DAC, MAC, RBAC, ABAC, and least privilege
Security policies, governance basics, and change management fundamentals

units.title: Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Mitigations
units.gate: Given a log excerpt, alert, or short scenario, name the specific threat/attack/vulnerability at work, name the indicator that gives it away, and recommend a concrete mitigation.

objectives.text: Threat actors, motivations, and attack surfaces
Malware types: viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware, spyware, rootkits, botnets, logic bombs
Social engineering techniques: phishing variants, pretexting, tailgating, business email compromise
Network attacks: DoS/DDoS, on-path (MITM), spoofing, replay, DNS poisoning
Application and web attacks: injection, XSS, buffer overflow, race conditions (conceptual)
Vulnerability types: misconfigurations, zero-days, legacy systems, supply-chain and third-party risk
objectives.labPrompt: Run a permission-scoped Nmap scan of your own home network and record any unexpected open ports.

objectives.text: Indicators of compromise and threat-hunting fundamentals
Mitigation techniques and secure coding concepts: hardening, segmentation, input validation, patch management

units.title: Security Architecture
units.gate: Given a system design, identify a missing architectural control and explain what specific failure it prevents.

objectives.text: Defense-in-depth, network segmentation, and Zero Trust concepts
objectives.labPrompt: Sketch a segmentation diagram separating IoT, guest, and trusted devices into different VLANs/subnets.

objectives.text: Secure baselines and system hardening
objectives.labPrompt: Review your router's or laptop's settings against a basic hardening checklist.

objectives.text: Secure communication protocols: TLS, SSH, IPsec, DNSSEC
objectives.labPrompt: Run openssl s_client -connect <site>:443 and read which TLS version/cipher suite it negotiated.

objectives.text: Cloud and virtualization security: shared responsibility, containers, infrastructure as code
objectives.labPrompt: List which security controls are yours to configure vs the provider's under the shared-responsibility model on a free-tier cloud VM.

objectives.text: Identity and access management strategy in architecture: federation, privileged access management, just-in-time access
Endpoint, mobile, and embedded/IoT/ICS security considerations
objectives.labPrompt: Check how one IoT/embedded device you own receives firmware updates.

objectives.text: High availability and resilience design: redundancy, failover, and capacity planning
objectives.labPrompt: Sketch a redundant architecture and identify the single point of failure it removes.

units.title: Security Operations
units.gate: Given an incident scenario, correctly sequence the response, prioritize a vulnerability, or reason about an RTO/RPO or forensics constraint -- not just name the vocabulary.

objectives.text: Security monitoring, log analysis, and SIEM/SOAR fundamentals
objectives.labPrompt: Try a free SIEM sandbox and run one basic search query against sample log data.

objectives.text: Incident response process and the NIST incident response lifecycle
Threat intelligence sources and threat hunting in practice
Vulnerability management: scanning, CVSS scoring, and remediation prioritization
objectives.labPrompt: Look up a recent published CVE for an app/OS you use (nvd.nist.gov) and note its CVSS score.

objectives.text: Digital forensics basics: chain of custody, order of volatility, legal holds
objectives.labPrompt: Write a short chain-of-custody log template for a hypothetical piece of evidence.

objectives.text: Change management and configuration management processes
Business continuity and disaster recovery: BIA, RTO/RPO, backup types, DR sites
objectives.labPrompt: Draft a one-page BIA outline for a small hypothetical business.

objectives.text: Security tools in operation: firewalls, IDS/IPS, EDR, and DLP

units.title: Security Program Management and Oversight
units.gate: Given a governance or compliance scenario, name the right instrument and correctly reason about risk math or third-party exposure.

objectives.text: Governance frameworks and the policy/standard/procedure/guideline hierarchy
Risk assessment: qualitative vs quantitative analysis (ALE, SLE, ARO)
Third-party and supply-chain risk management
Security awareness training programs
Compliance, regulations, and audits (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS)
Security metrics, KPIs, and reporting to leadership
